## Introduction

This report summarises a small example dataset to demonstrate how Quarto combines **code**, **test**, and *results* in one document.

## The Data
```{r}
df = data.frame(
  group = c("A","A","B","B"),
  value = c(10,15,20,25)
)

df
```

## Summary

```{r}
avg_value = mean(df$value)
avg_value
```

The average value across all groups is `r avg_value`. This sentence used **inline code** to insert that number automatically.


## Visualization

```{r}
plot(runif(100), rnorm(100), main = "Nonsense")
```
---

## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
